Allenylation
Theoretical Studies of Allene Synthesis through Cadmium Iodide-
Mediated Allenylation of Terminal Alkynes
Yulin Han[a, b] and Xue Zhang*[a, b]
Abstract: The cadmium iodide-mediated reaction between
an amine and two molecules of terminal alkynes for the syn-
thesis of allenes has been investigated by using DFTc alcula-
tions. On the basis of these calculations,a plausible mecha-
nism has been proposed. Ther esultsa lso reveal that pyrroli-
dine serves not only as ar eactant but also as as huttle in a
proton relay.
Introduction
Allenes are an important class of compounds that serve as in-
valuables ynthons in synthetic organic chemistry,[1] and these
moieties have been found in many naturalp roductsa nd phar-
maceuticals.[1a] In the past, there has been much effort to de-
velop synthetic methods fort heir preparation.[2, 3] Amongt hese
approaches, the metal-promoted allenylationo ft erminal al-
kynes (ATA)w itha ldehydesi nt he presence of amines has
emergeda sa practical synthetic methodf or the construction
of substituted allenes.[3a, b, 4–6] By using ATAr eactions,
mono-,[3a, b, 4] 1,3-di-,[5] and trisubstituted allenes[6] are now
easily prepared from terminal alkynes, aldehydes or ketones,
and amines.
In terms of the mechanism, the formation of propargylamine
C from the A3-coupling[7, 8] of an alkyne,a ldehydeo rk etone,
and amine is one of the key steps (Scheme 1). This proceeds
through the reactiono f1 -alkynyl zinc species A with ketonimi-
nium ion B,w hich is generated in situ from the condensation
of the aldehyde with morpholine. After the formation of C,a
subsequent[ 1,5] hydride migration and b-elimination[9] pro-
duce the final allene product (i.e.,a ZnI2-promoted ATAr eac-
tion, Scheme 1).[9] This mechanism is supported by our detailed
theoreticali nvestigations.[9a]
Recently,a cadmium iodide-mediated tandem reaction that
involves an aminea nd two molecules of terminal alkynes for
the synthesis of trisubstituted allenes was developedb yo ur
group (Scheme 2).[10] It is worth noting that in contrast to the
classical ATAr eactions mentioneda bove,a ldehydes or ketones
are not necessary for the formation of allene by using this
method.I nt he absence of an aldehyde or ketone, propargyla-
mine C could not be formed through the A3-coupling process.
Consequently,t he above-mentionedm echanism is inapplicable
to this protocol, especially to the generation of ketoniminium
ion B.
With our continued interest in the development of synthetic
methodsf or the preparation of allenes,[4a, c–g, 5a–g, 6] anda subse-
quent desire to understand their mode from am echanistic
perspective,[9] we proceeded to performa computational in-
vestigation of this CdI2-mediated ATA reactiont hat involves an
amine and twot erminal alkyne molecules.

Results and Discussion
In the absence of an aldehyde or ketone, the ketoniminium
ion can be generated by the hydroamination of an alkyne.[11]
The calculated free energy profiles for the hydroaminationo f
propyne with pyrrolidine are provided in Figure 1, and the
generation of both Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov prod-
ucts has been investigated in detail. The depicteds tructures of
the stationary pointsa longt he schematic of the Markovnikov
pathway are illustrated in Figure 1.[12]
The initial formation of the complex Int1 (selected as af ree
energy reference) generated by the simultaneous coordination
of the pyrrolidinea nd alkyne to CdI2 leads to ad ecrease in
energy by 20.7 kcal mol@1.C omplex Int1 is at etrahedral four-
coordinate CdII complex. The coordination of CdII to the C1@C2
triple bond of the alkyne resultsi nt he lengthening of the
bond from 1.200 a (for 1a without CdII coordination)t o
1.215 a (in Int1). Thus, the coordination of CdII reduces the
strength of the triple bond and increases its reactivity towards
nucleophilic attack by pyrrolidine. Natural bond orbital (NBO)
analysisr eveals that the Wiberg bond index of the C1@C2
triple bond in Int1 is 2.81, which is smaller than that of C1@C2
triple bond in 1a (2.91). This differencei st he result of the
bonding p electrons of the triple bond being donated to the
empty orbitalo fC dII and CdII backdonating its de lectrons into
the empty antibonding orbital (p*) of the triple bond. When
the subsequent pyrrolidine attack takes place at the C1 atom
of the alkyne, the Markovnikovp roduct is produced (solid line
in Figure 1). In contrast, the anti-Markovnikov product is pro-
vided when the C2 atom participatesi nt he attack (dotted line
in Figure1 ). The nucleophilic attack that proceeds through the
Markovnikovp athway is endergonic (DGsol = 10.4 kcal mol@1)
and requiresaf ree energy barrier of 25.6 kcal mol@1 (TS1_1),
which is lower than TS1_2 for the anti-Markovnikov attack by
2.4 kcal mol@1 (28.0 kcal mol@1).
The expected enamine Int6_1 of the Markovnikov pathway
could be formed by ap roton migration from the amine N1
atom to the C2 atom of zwitterionic intermediate Int2_1.H ow-
ever,t he activatione nergy of this direct protont ransfer is com-
puted to be 50.9 kcal mol@1 (TS2’)w ith respect to Int2_1,
which suggestst hat this step is not kinetically favorable. The
ring strain of the four-membered cyclic structure of TS2’ may
lead to its highe nergy.
Ak inetically more favorable pathway fort he protont ransfer,
which is assisted by an additional pyrrolidine molecule, has
been discovered.[11d, 13] Intermediate Int3_1 is strongly stabi-
lized (15.6 kcal mol@1)b yt he formation of two hydrogen bonds
to an additional pyrrolidine molecule [d(N2···H1) = 1.789 a and
d(I···H2) = 3.030 a]. The subsequent abstractiono ft he H1
proton from the N1 atom and transfer to the N2 atom (in
Int3_1)r equiresa free energyb arriero fo nly 1.5 kcal mol@1
(TS2_1)t oa fford the pyrrolidiniumi on intermediate Int4_1.
This process is exergonic relative to Int3_1 by 6.9 kcal mol@1.
Subsequently,t he proton from the pyrrolidinium ion under-
goes another migration to the C2 alkyne carbon to produce
enamine-bound intermediate Int5_1.T his step is calculatedt o
be highly exergonic (38.6 kcal mol@1 relative to Int4_1)a nd re-
quires af ree energyb arrier of only 3.9 kcal mol@1.F inally,e n-
amine Int6_1 is released from coordination to the CdI2 to com-
plete this alkyne hydroamination process. Thus, our calcula-

tions show that the assistance of an extra pyrrolidinem olecule
changes the direct protont ransfer to ai rreversible stepwise
protonation–deprotonation process that is highly exergonic by
45.5 kcal mol@1 (Int5_1 relative to Int3_1)a nd requires at otal
free energy barrier of only 3.9 kcal mol@1,w hichi sa significant
reduction in the activatione nergy.
The hydroamination of an alkyne through an anti-Markovni-
kov pathway is shown for comparision (dotted line in Figure 1,
for detailss ee Supporting Information, Figure S1).T he comput-
ed potential energy surface is qualitativelys imilart ot hat of a
Markovnikov process, but this pathway is more energy de-
manding, especially the step for the nucleophilic attack
(28.0 kcal mol@1 for TS1_2 vs. 25.6 kcal mol@1 for TS_1). Thus,
Markovnikov intermediate Int2_1 is generated overwhelmingly.
It is worth noting that the coordination of CdI2 to the alkyne
triple bond of Int1 is unsymmetrical with al onger Cd···C1
(2.995 a)t han Cd···C2 distance (2.692 a), which indicates that
the terminal C2 carbon is more strongly coordinated to the
cadmium center than the substituted C1 carbon. Moreover,
natural population analysis( NPA) reveals that the natural
atomic chargeo nt he C2 atom of Int1 is much more negative
than that on the C1 atom (@0.32 vs. 0.05 e),a nd, thus, the C2
carbon is less reactive than C1 atom towards nucleophilic
attack by pyrrolidine. Our investigation accountsf or the selec-
tivity of the alkyne hydroamination through the Markovnikov
pathway,w hich is also in accordance with the experimental
observations of the Markovnikovp roduct as the sole prod-
uct.[10]
Propargylamine is one of the key intermediates in the syn-
thesis of allenes, and this has been verifiede xperimentally by
using this nonclassical ATAp rocess.[10] According to our under-
standing of ATAr eactions,[9a] propargylamine may be produced
by the electrophilic attack on the 1-alkynyl cadmium species
by the ketoniminium ion. In this process, the ketoniminium ion
is probablyg enerated by enamine protonation. Figure 2p res-
ents the free energy profile fort he generationo fp ropargyla-
mine from the initial complex Int1 (free energy reference). The
process starts with the isomerization of Int1 into Int7,i nw hich
two hydrogen bonds are formed between the pyrrolidine mol-
ecule and the alkyne-coordinated CdI2 [d(N1···H) = 1.921 a and
d(I···H1) = 3.071 a], and leads to an energy increase of 14.9 kcal
mol@1.T he C2@Hs ingle bond is weakened by the formationo f
hydrogenb onds, which results in an increase in the C2@H
bond distance by 0.040 a (1.109 a in Int7 vs. 1.069 a in Int1).
The subsequenta bstraction of the proton from the C2 carbon
of the terminala lkyne and transfer to the N1 atom of pyrroli-
dine (in Int7,F igure 2) requires an activation energy of 4.9 kcal
mol@1 (TS4)t oa fford complex Int8,w hich contains hydrogen-
bondingi nteractions between the 1-alkynyl cadmium species
and the pyrrolidiniumi on.
The in situ generated pyrrolidinium ion may then act as a
proton source for the conversion of the enamine intermediate
into ak etoniminium ion. This enamine protonation step is cal-
culated to require an activation energy of only 6.0 kcal mol@1
through TS5 to afford intermediate Int10,w hich is ah ydro-
gen-bonded complexo ft he ketoniminium ion, pyrrolidine,
and propyn-1-yl cadmium species. We tried to evaluatet he
possibility of the directp roton transfer from the terminal
alkynet ot he enamine, but we were unable to locate the tran-
sition-state structures of this transformationw ith or without
the assistance of CdI2.O bviously,t he two precursors for the
propargylamine formation, the propyn-1-yl cadmium species
and ketoniminium ion, could be easily generated with the as-
sistanceo fa pyrrolidine molecule. The pyrrolidine may act as a
protons huttleo nce againb ya bstracting ap roton from the
terminala lkyne carbona tom and subsequently protonating
the enamine to give ak etoniminium ion.
The reaction continued with the releaseo fp yrrolidine from
Int10 to yield the anion/cation complex Int11,w hich is ender-
gonic by 7.5 kcal mol@1 relative to Int10.T he subsequente lec-
trophilica ttack of the ketoniminium ion on the C2 atom at-
tachedt oc adium requires an energy barrier1 0.5 kcal mol@1
(TS6)t op rovide propargylamine-CdI2 complex Int12,w hich is
lower in energy by 1.8 kcal mol@1 relative to Int1.T he genera-
tion of propargylamine from Int1 can proceed smoothly with
the highest free energy barriero f1 9.8 kcal mol@1 (TS4). The
purpose of the CdI2 in this process is to activate the terminal
alkyne towards electrophilica ttack by the iminium ion.

Allene can be obtained from the propargylamine througha
CdI2-promoted [1,5] hydride migration and b-elimination step.
The pyrrolidine moiety of Int12,w ith its envelope conforma-
tion, has two axial hydrogen atoms (H2 and H3) that are per-
fectly oriented for migration to the C1 atom. The six-mem-
bered cyclic transition-state TS7 for the [1,5] hydride shift has
been located, and during this transformationa s bond be-
tween the CdII and C2 atom is formed to generate intermedi-
ate Int13.T his [1,5] hydride migration stepi sc omputed to be
slightly endergonic (DGsol = 4.1 kcal mol@1)a nd requires an acti-
vation barrier of 21.3 kcal mol@1 (relativet o Int12). The coordi-
nation with CdI2 enhances the reactivityo ft he propargylamine
by increasing the C1@C2 triple bond distance from 1.211 a
(withoutC dI2 coordination) to 1.222 a (in Int12). This increase
is the result of electron donation and back-donation between
the triple bond and cadmium(II) ion. Thus, the coordinationo f
CdI2 to the propargylamine in Int12 facilitates the subsequent
[1,5] hydride migration and b-elimination step. The b-elimina-
tion to give intermediate Int14 is relatively easier with an acti-
vation barrier of only 11.7 kcal mol@1 through TS8 (Figure 2).
The simultaneous breaking of the C@Na nd C@Cd bonds irre-
versibly provide the product Int14,w hich is 12.3 kcal mol@1
lower in energy than Int13.T he final step of the process in-
volves the releaseo f 3a from its coordination to cadmium.
The release of allene is calculated to be endergonic by 8.7 kcal
mol@1 to produce the CdI2-coordinated 3,4-dihydro-2H-pyrrole
Int15 and the final allene product 3a .T hus, during the forma-
tion of allene from propargylamine, the [1,5] hydride migration
step is computedt oh ave the highest relative energy barrier of
21.3 kcal mol@1 (TS7 relative to Int12). The key role of the CdI2
in this process is to activate the alkyne towards hydride migra-
tion.
It should be noted that the highest relative energy barrier
(21.3 kcal mol@1, TS7 in Figure 2) for the formation of allene by
the Int1 process (Figure 2) is lower than that of the process for
the formation of the enamine (25.6 kcal mol@1, TS1_1 in
Figure 1). If we only consider the energy barriers, it seemst hat
enaminef ormation should never take place. Nevertheless, the
formation of the allene requires the enamine as ar eactant to
form the thermodynamically more stable intermediates.
Conclusions
In summary,t he mechanism of this CdI2-mediated ATAr eaction
in the presence of an amine and two terminal alkynem ole-
cules was investigated in detail. On the basis of the DFT calcu-
lations,a modified reactionm echanism has been proposeda s
shown in Scheme 3. First, the CdI2-promoted hydroamination
of the alkyne by pyrrolidine produces the enamine according
to Markovnikov’s rule. The corresponding ketoniminium ion is
then obtainedb yp rotonation of the enamine. The ketonimini-
um ion undergoes ar eactionw ith the 1-alkynyl cadmium spe-
cies, obtained from at erminal alkyne in the presence of pyrro-
lidine, to provide the propargylamine. Finally,[ 1,5] hydride mi-
gration and b-elimination in the presence of CdI2 provides the
desired trisubstituted allene.B ecause the hydroamination of
the alkyne to form the enamine features the highest relative
energy barrier (25.6 kcal mol@1, TS1_1)o ft he entire process,
this is the rate-determining step. In particular,o ur investigation
suggestst hat pyrrolidine not only act as ar eactant but also as
as huttlei nt he proton relay process that occurs during the hy-
droamination of the alkyne and the formationo ft he propyn-1-
yl cadmium species and ketoniminium ion. Moreover,o ur cal-
culations reveal that the main role of CdI2 is to facilitatet he hy-
droamination reaction by activating the terminal alkyne and
accelerate the [1,5] hydride migration by activating the propar-
gylamine.
Experimental Section
Computational Methods:A ll calculations were carried out by
using the Gaussian 09[14] package. Geometries were fully optimized
by using the density functional theory B3LYP method[15].T he
LANL2DZ basis set[16] with effective core potential (ECP) was used
for the Cd and Ia toms, and the 6-31G (d)[16b, 17] basis set was used
for the other atoms. Harmonic vibration frequency calculations
were conducted at the same level of theory to verify the stationary
points as minima (no imaginary frequency) or saddle points (one
imaginary frequency). Intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC)[18] calcula-
tions were performed to confirm the connection of the transition-
state structures with their corresponding reactants and products.
The single point energies and solvent effects in toluene were com-
puted by M06[19]/SDD-6-311 + G(d,p) basis sets using the SMD[20]
solvation model. All of the energies discussed in this paper are
Gibbs free energies at 298 K( DGsol)i nt oluene [dielectric constant
(e) = 2.37],u nless otherwise specified. Fully optimized structures
are illustrated using CYLView.W eu tilized propyne (1a ,R = Me in
Scheme 2) as the working model of the terminal alkyne to reduce
the computational cost.
